step_notes.s8: Boundary analysis uses separate parameter regimes, rather than all the active strict-margin premises simultaneously. For delta=0 retain x!=0 and ||x-y||<=delta; then y=x. For the equality-threshold witness, REPLACE delta<||x|| by delta=||x|| and take y=0, so N(y) is undefined. For x=0, REPLACE the active x!=0 premise; for dimension zero, REPLACE d>=1 by d=0. These last regimes lie outside the normalization theorem domain. The i2/s3 links provide context for what changes; they are not strict-margin implications proving the excluded cases.

step_notes.s12: Separate valid specializations from excluded-domain diagnostics. For epsilon=0 retain s>0: the exact nonzero branch has p=s^2/alpha^2. For s=0, REPLACE s>epsilon from i4 by s=0 while retaining alpha>0, epsilon>=0, the operator-error promise, unitarity and ||psi||=1. Do not import the positive-success conclusion of s6 into this branch: Apsi/s is undefined; epsilon=0 gives p=0, and epsilon>0 gives only p<=min(1,(epsilon/alpha)^2). For m=0 or n=0, retain the original valid margin premises: m=0 gives P=I and p=1; n=0 gives a one-dimensional complex system, not the zero vector space. The i4/s6 references in the raw endpoint node are contextual, not simultaneous assumptions for the s=0 diagnostic.

grading_notes: For rubric r2 and r3, accept either equivalent positive-alpha scaling. The reference route takes x=Apsi/alpha, y=Bpsi and delta=epsilon/alpha. A fully correct alternative takes x=Apsi, y=alpha Bpsi and delta=epsilon. The latter proves ||x-y||<=epsilon<s=||x||, hence x!=0 and alpha Bpsi!=0; alpha>0 then gives Bpsi!=0 and N(alpha Bpsi)=Bpsi/||Bpsi|| exactly. Applying the supplied lemma gives the same 2epsilon/s bound. Full credit does not require writing epsilon/alpha when the alternative route correctly preserves the stated norm convention and all nonzero premises.

inputs.statement: q is a real polynomial of degree at most the nonnegative integer d.
u:X->R and v:Y->R are arbitrary functions; F(x,y)=q(u(x)+v(y)).
Matrix multiplication over inner set {0,...,d} is a finite sum; for arbitrary outer sets algebraic rank is dimension of the column-function span.

steps.claim: Produce the exact shifted coefficients.
assumptions: Real polynomial, degree bound d.
steps.conclusion: For all real a,s, q(a+s)=sum_{i=0}^d c_i(a)s^i.
steps.justification: Finite binomial expansion and collection of equal powers; c_i(a)=sum_{k=i}^d a_k binom(k,i)a^(k-i).

steps.claim: Separate the row and column variables.
assumptions: The same q,u,v as in the question.
steps.conclusion: F(x,y)=sum_i c_i(u(x))v(y)^i.
steps.justification: Substitute a=u(x), s=v(y).

steps.claim: Assemble actual factors and verify equality.
assumptions: Finite inner sum, with no finiteness requirement on outer sets.
steps.conclusion: A(x,i)=c_i(u(x)), B(i,y)=v(y)^i satisfy F=AB with width d+1.
steps.justification: Unfold finite matrix multiplication entrywise.

steps.claim: Pass from the finite-width representation to rank.
assumptions: Columns are real functions on X.
steps.conclusion: rank F<=d+1.
steps.justification: Every column of F lies in the span of the d+1 columns of A.

steps.claim: Explain degree control and degenerate boundaries.
assumptions: d is only an upper degree bound; outer sets may be empty.
steps.conclusion: Width depends on d, while zero/constant/empty/repeated-value arrays may have smaller rank.
steps.justification: The finite powers determine I; no step uses an outer size, nonzero coefficient, distinct value or nonempty row/column premise.

inputs.statement: Finite real core slices, dimensions r_j and first-core-first products with scalar external bonds.
Internal G_j are invertible and G_0=G_n=I_1; B_j^s=G_{j-1}^{-1}A_j^sG_j.
S is the full finite word sum of squared scalar amplitudes and norm=sqrt(S).
For the conditional canonicality claim, sum_s A_j^s(A_j^s)^T=I at each core.
For the sufficient-condition branch, every internal G_j is orthogonal.
For the converse branch only, every transformed core is right-canonical.

steps.claim: Prove the prefix gauge invariant.
assumptions: Correct dimensions and adjacent inverses.
steps.conclusion: P_B,k=G_0^{-1}P_A,k G_k for 0<=k<=n.
steps.justification: Induct on k; base is the identity and the step cancels G_{k-1}G_{k-1}^{-1} by associativity.

steps.claim: Recover exact full scalar amplitudes.
assumptions: Both external gauges are identity.
steps.conclusion: For every word, f_B(s)=f_A(s).
steps.justification: Take k=n in the prefix invariant and apply the two endpoint identities.

steps.claim: Recover mass and norm.
assumptions: No nonzero assumption is needed for sums of squares or the nonnegative square root.
steps.conclusion: S_B=S_A and sqrt(S_B)=sqrt(S_A).
steps.justification: Substitute amplitude equality into each finite summand and take the same square root.

steps.claim: Compute the transformed local row-Gram.
assumptions: Real transpose reverses factor order.
steps.conclusion: Gram(B_j)=G_{j-1}^{-1}[sum_s A_j^s G_jG_j^T(A_j^s)^T]G_{j-1}^{-T}.
steps.justification: Expand each B_j^s(B_j^s)^T and pull out the factors independent of s.

steps.claim: Prove the orthogonal-gauge sufficient condition.
assumptions: Original train is right-canonical; gauges including endpoints are orthogonal.
steps.conclusion: Every transformed local Gram is identity.
steps.justification: Use G_jG_j^T=I, then original canonicality, then G_{j-1}^{-1}G_{j-1}^{-T}=I.

steps.claim: Prove orthogonality is necessary for two fully canonical trains.
assumptions: A is right-canonical and, for this converse, B is right-canonical; terminal gauge is identity.
steps.conclusion: Every internal G_j is orthogonal.
steps.justification: Backward induction from G_n=I: if G_jG_j^T=I, the A and B row-Gram identities force I=G_{j-1}^{-1}G_{j-1}^{-T}, hence G_{j-1}G_{j-1}^T=I.

steps.claim: Refute unrestricted canonicality preservation while confirming global invariance.
assumptions: n=2, all bonds one, A_j^0=1, A_j^1=0 and G_1=2 are legal inputs.
steps.conclusion: Input Grams are 1; output Grams are 4 and 1/4; the only nonzero scalar amplitude remains 1.
steps.justification: Direct substitution supplies an exact witness and uses both the amplitude and local-Gram branches.

steps.claim: Check empty and zero-dimensional gauge invariance without canonicality.
assumptions: Empty products and sums, and the identity/inverse on the zero vector space, have the meanings fixed in the question. No canonicality assumption is used in this branch.
steps.conclusion: For n=0 there is one empty word with scalar amplitude 1, squared mass 1 and norm 1. For n=1 no internal gauge exists and B=A. If an internal bond is zero, every full scalar contraction is zero for both trains, so both masses and norms are zero; the exact prefix and amplitude identities remain valid.
steps.justification: The empty contraction is I_1 and both endpoint gauges are I_1. For n=1 both gauges bordering the single core are identities. A full product crossing a zero-dimensional internal space is the zero 1-by-1 matrix; all gauge cancellations still hold with empty matrix identities. No normalization or nonzero/full-rank premise is introduced.

steps.claim: Check zero-bond impossibility only in the right-canonical branch.
assumptions: Assume the original train is fully right-canonical for this conditional branch only.
steps.conclusion: A fully right-canonical train with initial dimension r_0=1 cannot have any zero-dimensional internal bond. Thus the conditional canonicality preservation and converse claims have no realizable zero-bond input, while unconditional gauge invariance in C2-S7 still applies to zero-bond trains.
steps.justification: If a zero internal dimension existed, choose the first such bond. Its preceding dimension is positive because r_0=1 and all earlier bonds are positive. Both slices of the core entering the zero bond have zero output width, so their bit-summed row Gram is zero, contradicting the positive-dimensional identity required by C2-I4. This proof uses no gauge or nonzero-state assumption.

inputs.statement: Two finite real trains with common word order, common terminal dimension r, and possibly different intermediate bond dimensions.
H_n=I_r and H_{j-1}=sum_t A_j^t H_j(B_j^t)^T.
v,w are arbitrary initial column vectors; Phi values are the stated contractions, including all terminal labels.
For the Gram/PSD/kernel branch, A=B with matching bond dimensions.
There is one empty word, empty product I, and finite sums over empty bond labels are zero.

steps.claim: Prove the suffix cross-environment invariant.
assumptions: Matching physical and terminal indices; transpose reverses the product.
steps.conclusion: H_j=sum_{suffix words} P_A,>j P_B,>j^T for every j.
steps.justification: Backward induction: empty suffix gives I_r; distributing the update produces the sum over the current bit and tail word.

steps.claim: Read every cross entry and a flattened matrix representation.
assumptions: All terminal labels must be retained.
steps.conclusion: H_0(a,c)=sum_{s,b}P_A(s)_{ab}P_B(s)_{cb}, or H_0=U_A U_B^T.
steps.justification: Use the matrix-product entry formula and define U_A,U_B by columns (s,b).

steps.claim: Evaluate arbitrary initial-boundary cross-inner-products.
assumptions: No normalization or sign restriction on boundaries.
steps.conclusion: Phi_A(v)=U_A^T v and <Phi_A(v),Phi_B(w)>=v^T H_0 w.
steps.justification: Distribute finite sums, or multiply the displayed matrices with their exact dimensions.

steps.claim: Specialize to a symmetric positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.
assumptions: Identical trains.
steps.conclusion: E_0=U_A U_A^T is symmetric and v^T E_0 v=||Phi_A(v)||^2>=0.
steps.justification: Transpose the product and sum the squares of real output amplitudes.

steps.claim: Identify the entire kernel.
assumptions: Identical trains; no positive-definiteness assumption.
steps.conclusion: E_0 v=0 iff Phi_A(v)=0 coordinatewise.
steps.justification: Forward: zero quadratic form forces every squared coordinate zero. Reverse: U_A^T v=0 implies U_A U_A^T v=0.

steps.claim: Refute positivity for different trains.
assumptions: n=1 and all bond dimensions one; A^0=1,B^0=-1,A^1=B^1=0.
steps.conclusion: H_0=-1, a legal square cross environment with negative quadratic form.
steps.justification: Substitute the scalar slices; same-train premise is deliberately absent.

steps.claim: Check empty and zero-dimensional cross environments without identifying the trains.
assumptions: Retain the one-empty-word convention and finite sums over empty bond labels. The two trains may be different.
steps.conclusion: For n=0, p_0=q_0=r, H_0=I_r, Phi_A(v)=v, Phi_B(w)=w, and the pairing is v^T w. If r=0, an internal bond of either train is zero, or either full emitted map is zero, H_0=0. If p_0=0 or q_0=0, the corresponding initial vector and side of the rectangular identity are empty and the cross-pairing is zero. All formulas retain their specified dimensions.
steps.justification: At n=0 both ordered empty products are I_r. Empty terminal labels or a product through a zero internal space yield a zero emitted map. The representation H_0=U_A U_B^T then gives a zero cross environment whenever either factor is zero. Empty initial dimensions give the unique empty vector/empty row or column matrix. None of these conclusions uses A=B, canonicality, normalized boundaries or division by a norm.

steps.claim: Specialize the boundary cases to the identical-train Gram and its kernel.
assumptions: For this branch only assume A=B, with matching bond dimensions.
steps.conclusion: For n=0 the same-train Gram is I_r, the emitted norm is ||v|| and its kernel is {0}. When the full emitted map vanishes, including zero terminal/internal dimensions or a zero train, E_0=0 and every initial boundary lies in its kernel. A zero-dimensional initial space is covered by its unique vector. The general same-train Gram may be singular and need not be positive definite or entrywise nonnegative.
steps.justification: Under A=B, the unconditional cases of C3-S7 apply to E_0. Then C3-S4 identifies each quadratic form with output squared norm and C3-S5 identifies its entire kernel with coordinatewise vanishing emission. For n=0 emission is the identity on the terminal-labelled boundary, giving kernel {0}; for a zero output map every boundary emits zero. This conditional branch does not restrict the cross-environment cases in C3-S7. For the retained warning about entrywise signs, the legal one-core slices A^0=(1,-1)^T and A^1=(0,0)^T, with left dimension two and terminal dimension one, give E_0=[[1,-1],[-1,1]]. This is a same-train Gram with negative off-diagonal entries; the zero-output case already supplies singular Grams.

inputs.statement: d,M are finite natural numbers, basis B_{d,r} has the displayed polynomial formula, and every sample lies in [0,1].
Coefficient errors obey |ctilde_r-c_r|<=eta with eta>=0; raw vectors x,y are the evaluations at the same sample list.
The original squared sample mass satisfies ||x||^2>=m with m>0. This is the positive-mass component of original input C4-I3.

For the original strict-error route, eta sqrt(M)<sqrt(m). This is the strict-error component of original input C4-I3; the precision route proves the same inequality instead of assuming this component.
Euclidean norms and signed amplitudes are retained; empty samples give mass zero and zeroth powers evaluate to one.
For nonzero x,y in a finite-dimensional real or complex Euclidean space, ||x/||x||-y/||y|||| <= 2||x-y||/||x||; if ||x-y||<=delta<||x|| then y is nonzero.
For the precision branch 0<epsilon<2 and eta<=epsilon sqrt(m)/(2 sqrt(M)) after M>0 is established.
For the endpoint branch an endpoint is actually sampled and its corresponding original coefficient has magnitude at least a>0.

steps.claim: Establish the two basis facts.
assumptions: Real samples in [0,1]; degree d>=0.
steps.conclusion: B_{d,r}(t)>=0 and sum_{r=0}^d B_{d,r}(t)=1.
steps.justification: Nonnegative powers and binomial theorem; d=0 uses the constant polynomial convention.

steps.claim: Bound each evaluated error.
assumptions: All coefficient errors are bounded by eta.
steps.conclusion: |ptilde(t)-p(t)|<=eta for t in [0,1].
steps.justification: Triangle inequality and the nonnegative unit-sum weights.

steps.claim: Accumulate errors over the full sample list.
assumptions: There are M coordinates, including repetitions.
steps.conclusion: ||x-y||<=delta=eta sqrt(M).
steps.justification: Square the coordinate bounds, sum M terms and take nonnegative square roots.

steps.claim: Produce the original nonzero and feasible-dimension facts.
assumptions: Positive lower sample mass.
steps.conclusion: ||x||>=sqrt(m)>0 and M>=1.
steps.justification: Monotonicity of the square root; M=0 would give mass zero, contradicting m>0.

steps.claim: Obtain the perturbed-norm lower bound before choosing a strictness route.
assumptions: Only the proved raw-error bound and the original positive-mass lower bound are used; strictness is not assumed here.
steps.conclusion: ||y||>=||x||-||x-y||>=sqrt(m)-eta sqrt(M). This lower bound has not yet been asserted positive.
steps.justification: Apply the reverse triangle inequality, then substitute C4-S3 and the norm lower bound in C4-S4. Its sign is settled separately by either the original strict-error premise or the epsilon-precision route.

steps.claim: Produce a positive perturbed norm on the original strict-error route.
assumptions: Use the strict-error premise supplied for the original route. This premise is not imported into the separate precision route.
steps.conclusion: ||y||>=sqrt(m)-eta sqrt(M)>0, so y is nonzero on this route.
steps.justification: The strict inequality in C4-I3b makes the previously derived lower bound strictly positive. Together with C4-S3 and C4-S4 it also gives ||x-y||<=delta<||x||.

steps.claim: Compose the supplied normalization interface.
assumptions: Both vectors nonzero, same finite Euclidean space, and the verified raw error and original norm bounds.
steps.justification: Apply the supplied 2delta inequality, then substitute the proved numerator upper bound and positive denominator lower bound.

steps.claim: Derive strictness from coefficient precision without assuming the strict-error component.
assumptions: Use the target-precision branch 0<epsilon<2 and eta<=epsilon sqrt(m)/(2 sqrt(M)); M>0 is already proved from positive mass.
steps.conclusion: delta=eta sqrt(M)<=epsilon sqrt(m)/2<sqrt(m). Thus the precision condition supplies strict error-to-mass control without C4-I3b.
steps.justification: By C4-S4, sqrt(M)>0 and sqrt(m)>0. Multiply the precision inequality by sqrt(M) to cancel its positive denominator; epsilon<2 then gives strict inequality. C4-S3 supplies delta and the raw-error meaning.

steps.claim: Obtain nonzero y from the precision-derived strictness.
assumptions: Use only the precision route and the unconditional reverse-triangle bound.
steps.conclusion: ||y||>=sqrt(m)-eta sqrt(M)>0. More explicitly ||y||>=(1-epsilon/2)sqrt(m)>0 on the precision route.
steps.justification: Substitute the coefficient-precision estimate from C4-S7a into C4-S5a. Because 0<epsilon<2 and m>0 were retained by that route, the displayed lower bound is positive. This step has no dependency on C4-I3b or C4-S5.

steps.claim: Apply normalization stability on the precision route.
assumptions: Both vectors are nonzero in the same finite Euclidean space, with y nonzero supplied by precision-derived strictness.
steps.conclusion: ||x/||x||-y/||y||||<=2 eta sqrt(M/m) on the precision route.
steps.justification: Apply the explicitly supplied interface to nonzero x from C4-S4 and nonzero y from C4-S7b, then insert the common raw-error and original-norm bounds. This duplicates the legitimate interface application in C4-S6 under a different sufficient nonzero route; it does not require the original strict-error premise.

steps.claim: Conclude the requested epsilon accuracy from the precision route.
assumptions: Retain 0<epsilon<2 and the stated sufficient coefficient-precision bound.
steps.conclusion: The precision condition implies both y nonzero and normalized-state error at most epsilon, independently of assuming C4-I3b.
steps.justification: The nonzero conclusion is C4-S7b. By C4-S4 the factors sqrt(M) and sqrt(m) are positive; substitute eta<=epsilon sqrt(m)/(2 sqrt(M)) into the C4-S6p bound to obtain epsilon. The strict-error route C4-S5/C4-S6 and this route are alternative sufficient routes, never a conjunction.

steps.claim: Supply a concrete mass certificate from a sampled endpoint.
assumptions: An endpoint is sampled and its original coefficient magnitude is at least a.
steps.conclusion: p(0)=c_0, p(1)=c_d and m=a^2 is a valid positive lower mass.
steps.justification: Evaluate the basis at the endpoints; one squared coordinate supplies the bound, including d=0.

steps.claim: Demonstrate the shrinking-mass obstruction with all original premises realized.
assumptions: Instantiate d=1, M=2, samples 0 and 1, c=(a,0), ctilde=(a,a/2), eta=a/2 and m=a^2 for a>0. Instantiate the endpoint-magnitude premise at endpoint 0 with magnitude a.
steps.conclusion: x=(a,0), y=(a,a/2), ||x||^2=m=a^2 and eta sqrt(M)=a/sqrt(2)<a=sqrt(m). As a tends to zero, eta tends to zero but the normalized distance remains sqrt(2-4/sqrt(5))>0. Thus no mass-independent error guarantee vanishing with eta follows, even within the strict perturbation regime.
steps.justification: Use the endpoint identities from C4-S8, instantiated on this family, and compute both norms directly: normalized vectors are (1,0) and (2,1)/sqrt(5). The family itself supplies positive mass and strictness; neither the full stability conclusion nor its strict-error assumption is needed to construct this witness. C4-S3 identifies the same delta used in the strictness check.

steps.claim: Check raw zero-error, zero-mass and empty-sample boundaries without imposing positive mass.
assumptions: Use the raw polynomial/sample definitions and conventions. These boundary observations do not suppose a normalized state exists.
steps.conclusion: Signed coefficients and sample values are permitted. At d=0 the sole basis function is 1. If eta=0 then the coefficient rows, polynomial values and raw sample vectors agree. If the sampled mass is zero then x is the zero vector and x/||x|| is undefined. If M=0 both raw vectors are empty and the raw error bound is 0<=0.
steps.justification: Nonnegative unit Bernstein weights bound signed perturbations without changing signs. For d=0 the basis formula is identically 1. Eta=0 forces each coefficient error to vanish. A finite sum of real squares is zero precisely when all its coordinates vanish, including the empty-vector case. No division by sqrt(M) or by a zero norm is made.

steps.claim: Restrict normalized conclusions to the realizable positive-mass cases.
assumptions: For this branch retain the original positive-mass component. No strict-error component is needed for the zero-error or feasibility observations.
steps.conclusion: Under positive original mass, eta=0 gives equal nonzero raw vectors and normalized error zero. Zero sampled mass and M=0 contradict this branch and are not realizable examples of the normalized theorem. In particular the precision formula involving 1/sqrt(M) is used only with M>=1.
steps.justification: C4-S4 supplies nonzero x and M>=1. Combine this with the raw equality at eta=0 in C4-S10 to obtain y=x nonzero. Combine positive mass with the zero-mass facts of C4-S10 to exclude the contradictory cases, rather than normalizing an empty vector.
